newsitem.title: NIGERIA: More Nigerian banks move to raise capital bases.
newsitem.headline: More Nigerian banks move to raise capital bases.

text.p: More Nigerian banks are coming to the capital market for funds to meet a new minimum capital base set by the authorities, market operators said on Monday.

They said the Nigerian stock exchange had approved plans by Trans International Bank, Inland Bank and Trade Bank, which is already listed on the stock market, to increase their capital through new public issues.
Trans International Bank is raising 720 million naira ($8.8 million) through the issue of 720 million shares at 1.00 naira per share. The offer, which opened on Monday, closes on September 15.

Inland Bank wants to source 240 million naira by floating 200 million shares at 1.20 each while Trade Bank is seeking 420 million naira by selling 350 million shares at 1.20 naira apiece, operators said.
Banks have up to the end of 1998 to raise their capital to a minimum of 500 million naira, at least nine times the previous level.
Before the military government ordered the increase in January, the minimum capital for a commercial bank was 50 million naira and 40 million naira for merchant banks.

Nigeria's oldest bank, First Bank, first announced earlier this month the largest public issue so far this year to raise more than two billion naira through the sale of 200 million shares at 10.50 naira per share.
The issue is expected to be completed before the end of the year, according to one of the two joint issuing houses.
